fx-dm-alt: A flat ground with the volcano V and a station S a distance d apart, under a flat vault at height h. The pulse goes up, bounces off the vault and comes down to S. Seen in a mirror, the bounce is a straight line from V', the image of V at 2h above the ground, to S, so its length is L = √(d² + 4h²), longer the farther S is, whatever h
fx-kr-1: outer: III − I · inner: IV − II
fx-kr-alt: Left, a sphere with Krakatoa K and a barograph S. The wave passes S on its way out (I), runs on round the whole Earth and passes S again (III): III − I is one full lap, whatever the position of S. The wave coming back from the antipodes does the same the other way (II, then IV). Right, the seven passages actually read on the Glasgow barograph in 1883, on a time axis: the two laps, 36 h 36 min and 34 h 41 min, are bracketed
fx-kr-s: sphere schematic; time axis to scale
fx-tg-alt: Left, a sphere: from the volcano V the pressure wave reaches the station S the short way, over the angle θ, after t₁, and the long way, over 2π − θ, after t₂; the two paths add up to one full circumference, so t₁ + t₂ = 2πR/v wherever S is. Right, a plane: the wave is a circle that grows from V and crosses S once; nothing comes back from the other side
tg-v-alt: Band-passed pressure at 102 US weather stations, one line per station placed at its angle from the volcano, against hours after the eruption. Two bands of pulses run across the plot: the first arrives later the farther the station, the second arrives earlier the farther the station, as the globe predicts for a wave coming the short way and then the long way round. The flat model's best line has only the first.
tg-r-alt: Earth's radius computed separately at each station, against its angle from the volcano: from the first passage (open circles) and from the second (dots), with 6,371 km dashed. The dots sit in a narrow band just above the line and drift slightly downward with the angle; excluded stations are grey.
tg-r-s: v = 310 m/s, t₀ = 0; off-scale: at the edge
tg-read-flat: best plane, first passage: {x}× the globe's scatter
tg-row-a1: first passage, R = v t₁ / θ
tg-row-a2: second passage, R = v t₂ / (2π − θ)
tg-row-free: both on one line, t₀ left free
tg-fl-globe0: globe, nothing fitted (R = 6,371 km, v = 310 m/s)
tg-fl-rim: plane, second passage as an echo off a rim at {r} km
tg-v-dome: dome bounce (○): nearly flat, tilted the wrong way
tg-res-alt: The radius found, on a ruler in kilometres: a dot at {r} km, a dark bar for the statistical uncertainty alone, a wide pale band for the total uncertainty at one standard deviation and a thinner one at 95%, small ticks for each alternative reduction, and the mean radius of 6,371 km dashed, inside the band.
tg-res-ci: 95% confidence: {lo} – {hi} km · the mean radius, 6,371 km, lies {z} σ away
tg-res-parts: statistical ± {st} km ({n} stations) · systematic ± {sy} km, mostly the wave's speed (the two eruptions differ by 1.1 %)
tg-res-flatline: flat models, tuned in their favour: no radius, and a scatter {x}× the globe's (best: a dome {h} km high)
tg-fl-dome: plane, second passage bounced off a dome {h} km high (best height)
kr-lap-alt: The time of one complete lap of the Earth, measured at each 1883 barograph between two passages of the same wave, against the station's angle from Krakatoa. Laps towards the antipodes (dots) take about 36.2 hours, laps coming back (open circles) about 34.7 hours, at every distance: the lap does not depend on where the station is. The globe's lap with nothing fitted, 35.9 hours, is dashed between them.
kr-lap-x: station's angle from Krakatoa, θ (not used for the lap)
kr-lap-y: one lap of the Earth, hours
kr-gap-alt: The hours between the first and the second passage of the wave at each station, against its angle from Krakatoa. The points fall on a straight line, from 28 hours near Krakatoa to 7 hours near its antipodes, as the globe predicts with nothing fitted (dashed). The flat model's best echo off a rim (orange dots) and best bounce off a dome (orange open circles) scatter far from the measured points.
kr-gap-flat: plane at its best: • rim echo, ○ dome bounce
kr-gap-y: hours from passage I to passage II
kr-res-alt: The radius found from the 1883 barographs, on a ruler in kilometres: a dot at {r} km, a dark bar for the statistical uncertainty alone, a wide pale band for the total uncertainty at one standard deviation and a thinner one at 95 %, small ticks for each alternative reduction, and the mean radius of 6,371 km dashed, inside the band.
kr-res-parts: statistical ± {st} km ({n} stations) · systematic ± {sy} km: the gap fit and the wave's speed (the two eruptions differ by 1.1 %)
kr-res-flatline: flat models, tuned in their favour: no lap at all, and on the first interval a scatter {x}× the globe's
kr-read-n: {n} barographs of 1883, {k} with a lap each way
kr-read-lap: laps: {o} towards the antipodes, {b} coming back
kr-row-first: first lap each way, (III − I + IV − II) / 2
kr-row-out: towards the antipodes only (wind not cancelled)
kr-row-gap: interval I → II against θ, R/v fitted
kr-fl-rim: plane, II as an echo off a rim at {r} km
kr-fl-dome: plane, II bounced off a dome {h} km high (best height)
